findings.title: Migration Architecture Properly Delegates to Framework Layer
findings.description: The legacy destructive-command-guard plugin correctly delegates to the framework mutation-risk layer without duplicating logic or creating bypass paths.

evidence.analysis: Legacy plugin imports createFrameworkMutationRiskLayer from framework and returns its hook directly. No standalone logic remains that could diverge from framework behavior.

findings.recommendation: Current implementation is correct. No changes needed.

findings.title: Rule IDs and User-Facing Messages Preserved
findings.description: All destructive command rule IDs, severities, and error messages remain stable and unchanged in the reused rules.ts module.

evidence.analysis: Rules module is imported and re-exported from framework adapter. Tests confirm identical rule IDs: rm.recursive-force, git.checkout-discard, git.reset-hard, docker.system-prune, kubectl.delete-namespace, etc. Error message format unchanged.

findings.recommendation: Current implementation is correct. No changes needed.

findings.title: Environment Configuration Behavior Preserved
findings.description: Configuration parsing from environment variables uses identical logic and defaults via configFromEnv function.

evidence.analysis: Framework layer calls configFromEnv(options.env) with same environment variable names: OPENCODE_DESTRUCTIVE_GUARD_MODE, OPENCODE_DESTRUCTIVE_GUARD_EXTENDED, OPENCODE_DESTRUCTIVE_GUARD_ALLOW_TMP_RM_RF. Default values unchanged.

findings.recommendation: Current implementation is correct. No changes needed.

findings.title: Logging and Monitoring Preserved
findings.description: Security-relevant logging uses same service identifier and includes all critical context fields.

evidence.analysis: Logging uses service='destructive-command-guard' consistently. Logs include mode, callID, sessionID, ruleId, severity, and truncated command for audit trails.

findings.recommendation: Current implementation is correct. No changes needed.

findings.title: Cutover Contract Invariants Defined and Respected
findings.description: Legacy surface manifest defines clear invariants preventing dual activation and ensuring atomic cutover.

evidence.analysis: EPISTEMOLOGY_FRAMEWORK_LAYER_META.migrationStatus = 'mutation-risk-bash-adapter' tracks migration state. Cutover contract defines noDualActivation and atomicCutover invariants. Framework barrel (plugin/epistemology-framework.ts) does not exist yet, ensuring no dual activation risk.

findings.recommendation: Ensure future cutover PR follows contract invariants exactly - framework barrel activation must retire all legacy barrels atomically.

findings.title: Layer Ordering Places Mutation-Risk Last for Final Enforcement
findings.description: Mutation-risk layer is positioned at the end of layer order, ensuring it runs after policy and provenance layers.

evidence.analysis: EPISTEMOLOGY_FRAMEWORK_LAYER_ORDER = ['policy', 'worldview', 'provenance', 'mutation-risk']. Mutation-risk runs last in tool.execute.before sequence, providing final enforcement opportunity.

findings.recommendation: Current ordering is appropriate. Mutation-risk should remain last to catch any commands that pass through other layers.

key_assurances: Rule evaluation logic unchanged - rules.ts reused verbatim
Configuration parsing identical - same env vars and defaults
User-facing error messages preserved with stable rule IDs
Logging maintained with same service identifier
No dual activation risk - framework barrel not yet discoverable
Layer ordering appropriate - mutation-risk runs last for final enforcement
residual_risks: Future cutover must follow atomic activation contract
Ensure no environment variable drift during cutover testing
